title: Can the system dynamics remain structurally non-Markovian while its experimentally accessible memory signatures disappear?
authors: Sayan Sengupta, Anish Sharma, George Biswas, Anindya Biswas
abstract: We investigate how unresolved quasistatic disorder in system bath coupling affects non-Markovian dynamics in spin environments. The coupling is fixed within each experimental shot but varies between shots, so repeated shot tomography reconstructs a disorder averaged dynamical map. For a single spin bath with pure dephasing Ising interaction, disorder can drive a transition to CP-divisible dynamics for fixed bath preparations, with a critical strength set by bath polarization along the interaction axis. However, when the bath state fluctuates physically between shots, the averaged dynamics remain CP indivisible at any finite disorder strength. We extend these results analytically to inhomogeneously coupled pure dephasing baths of any number \(N\) of non-interacting spins. At any finite disorder strength, one unpolarized bath spin suffices to retain CP-indivisible dynamics, whereas a fully polarized bath yields Markovian (CP-divisible) dynamics. Dynamics with physically fluctuating bath states likewise remain non-Markovian (CP indivisible) at finite disorder for arbitrary \(N\) in the pure dephasing case. For anisotropic Heisenberg interactions, any nonzero transverse exchange eliminates the disorder driven transition to CP divisibility in a single spin bath. Exact diagonalization of anisotropic models with inhomogeneous couplings up to \(N=12\) reveals persistent trace distance revivals for fixed bath preparations, sampled Haar random preparations, and physically fluctuating bath states, showing that this effect of transverse exchange extends beyond a single bath spin. Increasing disorder still suppresses experimentally accessible revivals and can make memory effects unresolvable at finite measurement resolution even as the dynamics remain CP indivisible. Thus, transverse exchange and physical bath state fluctuations preserve dynamical indivisibility against unresolved coupling disorder.
summary: This theoretical study explores the resilience of non-Markovian quantum dynamics when the coupling to the environment is subject to unresolved disorder. The authors demonstrate that while disorder can make memory effects unresolvable, the underlying structural non-Markovianity can be preserved, particularly when considering physical bath state fluctuations or transverse coupling terms.
main_problem: The paper investigates whether a quantum system's dynamics can remain structurally non-Markovian (CP indivisible) even when the memory effects become experimentally unresolvable due to unresolved quasi-static disorder in the system-bath coupling.
main_result: Transverse exchange interactions and physical fluctuations in the bath state are shown to preserve the structural non-Markovianity (CP indivisibility) against disorder, even when memory signatures are suppressed.
method: The analysis uses process tomography to reconstruct disorder-averaged dynamical maps and employs CP divisibility as the primary criterion to distinguish between Markovian and non-Markovian dynamics.
model_or_system: The system is an open quantum system, specifically a spin environment (bath) coupled to a system spin. The coupling is modeled as a quasi-static random variable drawn from a Gaussian distribution, and the analysis compares pure dephasing Ising interactions with anisotropic Heisenberg interactions.
key_observables: CP divisibility, return probability ($P_R$), $\ell_1$-norm of coherence, and memory revivals.
important_parameters: Disorder strength ($\epsilon$), bath polarization, and the presence/absence of transverse exchange coupling.
main_assumptions: The analysis distinguishes between the disorder-averaged map and the true realization-resolved dynamics, and notes that the disappearance of memory signatures does not imply CP divisibility.
paper_structure: The paper develops its argument by analyzing the pure dephasing case (fixed vs. fluctuating bath states) and then extends the findings to anisotropic Heisenberg interactions, using analytical extensions and exact diagonalization to confirm the robustness of non-Markovianity.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses the crucial gap between theoretical structural properties (CP divisibility) and experimental observability (memory signatures) in open quantum systems, which is a major focus in quantum information and AMO physics.
